newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends firm, hits new contract high.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends firm, hits new contract high.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures closed firmer but off the new lifetime highs made across the board amid early mixed buying, floor sources said.

Trade buying on the open carried second-position March to a high of 11.90 cents. The benchmark October contract opened unchanged but broke through its previous high fo 11.65 cents and climbed to 11.70 on the reopen amid fund buying.
Producer pricing nudged prices off highs but steady buying kept the market over unchanged through the close, dealers said.

The benchmark October contract settled 0.07 cent higher at 11.63 cents a lb, having ranged from 11.70 to 11.55 cents. March finished up 0.11 at 11.90 cents, just under the lifetime high of 11.91 reached just ahead of the close.
The rest of the board ended 0.11 to 0.15 cent firmer.
"I think the market is acting constructively," Merrill Lynch sugar broker Tony Passimenti, said.

He noted that the market has managed to make new highs in the face of negative factors such as huge open interest in the most-active October contract, a lack of physical offtake, and steady selling by the trade.
Open interest in October stood at 109,700 lots as of early Thursday out of a total open interest of 181,693. March stood at 52,234 lots.
Dealers said the funds could continue their buying spree if the October contract breaks today's high of 11.70 cents, where stops may be resting.
An estimated 23,110 lots changed hands on the day compared with Thursday's official 16,407 lots.
